title: Existence of Kraus decomposition in infinite dimension via strongly-convergent direct process tomography
abstract: An algorithm is presented for Kraus decomposition of a completely positive operator over separable (countably-infinite-dimensional) Hilbert spaces, together with an elementary proof that the generated sum convergences in strong-operator topology. This improves on the standard, nonconstructive, proof by fusing the abstract problem with practical process tomography. Kraus operators are generated one-by-one, each having one more guaranteed zero matrix entry than the previous one. In this way, the stream of outputs of the algorithm provides a coherent family of Kraus decompositions of restrictions of the target CP map to ever-larger subspaces.
summary: This paper introduces a constructive algorithm to find the Kraus decomposition for completely positive maps acting on infinite-dimensional quantum systems. By employing direct process tomography and leveraging strong convergence arguments, it overcomes limitations of previous non-constructive proofs. This provides a powerful, systematic tool for analyzing open quantum evolution in complex physical settings.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop a constructive algorithm for finding the Kraus decomposition of a completely positive (CP) operator acting on separable, countably-infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
main_result: The authors present an elementary and practical algorithm that successfully constructs the Kraus operators and proves that their sum converges in the strong-operator topology (SOT).
method: The method combines direct process tomography with iterative reduction steps, systematically generating Kraus operators one by one while ensuring convergence properties.
model_or_system: The system involves quantum channels or CP maps ($\Lambda$) acting between separable Hilbert spaces ($H$ and $K$). The decomposition seeks to express $\Lambda$ as a sum of processes generated by Kraus operators: $\Lambda = \sum_{i=1}^{\infty} \Theta(A_i)$.
key_observables: The CP map ($\Lambda$), the resulting Kraus operators ($A_i$), and the convergence of the partial sums in SOT.
important_parameters: Separable (countably-infinite-dimensional) Hilbert spaces, orthonormal bases for $H$ and $K$.
main_assumptions: The proof relies on extending finite-dimensional results using density arguments involving nested projections ($P_\sigma$) and convergence in the trace norm ($\|\cdot\|_{1,1}$).
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing necessary tools (like the quasi-Cauchy-Schwarz inequality) to first solve the problem for finite dimensions before extending the constructive algorithm and proof of convergence to the infinite-dimensional case.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, algorithmic approach to decomposing quantum operations in infinite dimensions, which is crucial for modeling open quantum systems where continuous variables or infinite degrees of freedom are involved.
